answer_text:
# Computing $H_2(\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{Z})$ with Trivial Action

## Setting Up the Problem

Since $\mathbb{Q}$ (the additive group of rationals) is **abelian**, its classifying space is $K(\mathbb{Q}, 1)$. For any abelian group $A$, the group homology with trivial $\mathbb{Z}$-coefficients is given by exterior powers:

$$H_n(A, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \bigwedge\nolimits^n A \quad \text{for } n \geq 1$$

In particular:
$$H_2(\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Q} \wedge \mathbb{Q} = (\mathbb{Q} \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Q}) \,/\, \langle a \otimes a : a \in \mathbb{Q} \rangle$$

## Computing $\mathbb{Q} \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Q}$

Since $\mathbb{Q}$ is a **localization** of $\mathbb{Z}$ (at all nonzero integers), the standard localization identity gives:

$$\mathbb{Q} \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Q} \cong \mathbb{Q}, \qquad \text{via } \frac{a}{b} \otimes \frac{c}{d} \;\longmapsto\; \frac{ac}{bd}$$

Under this isomorphism, each generator $a \otimes a$ maps to $a^2 \in \mathbb{Q}$.

## Identifying the Subgroup $\langle a^2 : a \in \mathbb{Q} \rangle$

I need to determine the **additive subgroup** of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by all rational squares. Key observation:

$$\frac{1}{n} = n \cdot \left(\frac{1}{n}\right)^{\!2} \in \left\langle a^2 : a \in \mathbb{Q} \right\rangle \quad \text{for every } n \geq 1.$$

Since $1 = 1^2$ is also in the subgroup, all integers are included. Therefore, for any rational $\frac{p}{q}$:

$$\frac{p}{q} = p \cdot q \cdot \left(\frac{1}{q}\right)^{\!2} \in \left\langle a^2 : a \in \mathbb{Q} \right\rangle.$$

This proves $\langle a^2 : a \in \mathbb{Q} \rangle = \mathbb{Q}$ (the entire additive group).

## Final Quotient

$$\mathbb{Q} \wedge \mathbb{Q} \;=\; \mathbb{Q} \,/\, \mathbb{Q} \;=\; 0$$

## Verification with Known Cases

| Abelian group $A$ | $A \wedge A$ | $H_2(A,\mathbb{Z})$ | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\mathbb{Z}$ | $0$ | $0$ | $S^1$ has $H_2=0$ ✓ |
| $\mathbb{Z}^2$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ | $T^2$ has $H_2=\mathbb{Z}$ ✓ |
| $\mathbb{Z}/n$ | $0$ | $0$ | $K(\mathbb{Z}/n,1)$ has $H_2=0$ ✓ |
| $\mathbb{Q}$ | $0$ | $0$ | Consistent ✓ |

## Result

$$\boxed{H_2(\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{Z}) = 0}$$
